html:
Gum arabic is a natural resin collected from acacia trees, above all Acacia senegal, across the gum belt of the Sahel, and Sudan has long been the world's largest producer.

Farmers in Kordofan and Darfur tap the trees in the dry season and collect the hardened drops of sap. The gum is used to bind and thicken soft drinks, sweets, medicines, inks and paints, and was traded across the Sahara and down the Nile for centuries.

It was a leading export of Anglo-Egyptian Sudan. When the United States imposed sanctions on Sudan in 1997, gum arabic was exempted because American industry depended on it. The trade, like farming of sorghum, is a mainstay of rural Sudan.
sum: Gum arabic is a natural resin collected from acacia trees, above all Acacia senegal, across the gum belt of the Sahel, and Sudan has long been the world's largest producer.
